name: Laser Fault Injection
description: Use of focused laser beams to inject faults into integrated circuits with high spatial and temporal precision. Covers laser station operation, backside and frontside injection through thinned substrates, single-bit and multi-bit fault induction, laser scanning for fault mapping, and exploitation of laser-induced faults for key extraction and security bypass. Provides the highest spatial and temporal precision among fault injection techniques used in security evaluation.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to laser fault injection

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands laser fault injection principles and its role in security evaluation
evidence: Can explain how laser irradiation generates electron-hole pairs in silicon and how this induces transient currents that cause faults
Understands frontside vs. backside injection and why substrate thinning is necessary
Aware of laser FI station components (laser source, optics, positioning, triggering)
Understands laser safety classifications and lab safety requirements

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Operates laser fault injection station on prepared samples under supervision
evidence: Safely operates the laser FI station following all lab safety protocols (laser safety interlocks, PPE)
Aligns a prepared (decapped, thinned) sample on the laser station stage
Performs laser scanning to identify fault-susceptible regions on a training target
Induces targeted faults at specific timing windows using external trigger synchronization

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently performs laser FI campaigns with precise spatial and temporal targeting
evidence: Prepares samples for laser FI including backside thinning coordination with sample prep team
Performs laser fault mapping to identify individual register bits and SRAM cells
Exploits laser-induced single-bit faults for DFA key extraction on AES/RSA implementations
Bypasses security checks by targeting specific control-flow logic with laser FI
Completed laser FI assessments on 3+ distinct target ICs

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Performs advanced laser FI on hardened targets; develops attack strategies; mentors team
evidence: Defeats laser fault injection sensors and countermeasures (light sensors, mesh shields)
Performs multi-spot and multi-pulse laser FI attacks on complex targets
Correlates laser FI results with IC layout analysis for targeted attacks on specific modules
Develops automated laser scanning and fault characterization workflows
Mentors team on sample preparation, laser station operation, and fault exploitation

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on laser FI; publishes research; defines evaluation methodology
evidence: Published research on novel laser FI techniques at CHES, FDTC, or equivalent conferences
Defines the lab's laser FI methodology aligned with Common Criteria and EMVCo evaluation standards
Specifies and commissions laser FI station configurations for the lab
Provides expert consultation on laser FI resistance to smart card and secure IC designers

assessment_methods.description: Perform laser FI on a prepared target IC: map fault-susceptible regions, achieve single-bit fault precision, and demonstrate key extraction via DFA or security bypass
Observe laser safety compliance, sample alignment technique, scanning methodology, and fault characterization during a live laser FI session

equipment: Laser fault injection station (e.g., Riscure Laser Station, Hamamatsu PHEMOS)
IR laser source (1064nm) for backside injection
Visible laser source (532nm) for frontside injection
